title: Sunny and the Moonlit Meadow | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka walks out into a wide open moonlit meadow and finds that when you stand in the middle of it with nothing overhead but the whole sky, the whole world feels possible. A gentle final bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The meadow opened up.

Sunny had been in the bush for a while — enclosed by trees, by wattles, by the close comfort of the understorey — and then the trees parted and the meadow was there. Wide and flat and silver in the full moonlight, the grass pale, the air softer somehow without the trees to hold it in.

She walked out.

Further. Further. Into the middle.

The trees were behind her now on all sides, far enough away to be a dark ring at the edge of things. Above her, the whole sky. The full moon. The stars.

She had not realised how long she had been under trees.

She spread her arms and turned slowly.

The meadow was enormous. She was very small. The sky was bigger than she could take in at once. She tried anyway — turning slowly, tilting back — trying to hold all of it.

She thought: this is what it feels like when nothing is in the way.

She sat down in the very centre of the meadow.

The full moon shone directly down on her. The stars surrounded her. The grass was soft and the air was still and the sky was the biggest ceiling she had ever had.

She lay back.

The meadow held her, wide and silver and open.

The stars held the meadow.

And the night held all of it, together, gently.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, moonlit meadow. Goodnight, little one.
